name: F: One-shot generation with mean-reversion loss
theory: I2 proved GT is strongly mean-reverting (VR=0.21 at h=30) while model is super-diffusive (VR=0.51). AR frame-by-frame may dilute h=30 gradient through 30 sequential operations. One-shot Conv3D decoder (already exists in codebase as SinglePassDecoder) generates all 30 frames at once — CRPS loss at h=30 has direct gradient to the decoder. Combined with a variance ratio loss that penalizes VR>GT, this directly targets the mean-reversion gap.
prediction: Variance ratio at h=30 should decrease toward GT 0.21. Per-horizon CI should be more uniform. Growing uncertainty should still pass (one-shot can learn it from the CRPS trajectory).
risk: The Conv3D one-shot decoder was abandoned early (Exp 89) because it lacked temporal coherence. May need to re-validate surface validity. Also increases model params (Conv3D backbone is bigger than FrameDecoder MLP).
implementation: Reactivate SinglePassDecoder with afCRPS loss. Add VR loss: penalize var(sum of h changes) / (h * var(1-change)) at h=10,20,30 when it exceeds GT values.

name: G: Per-cell condition fan-out
theory: I1 proved encoder uses ~5 of 128 dims with 123 spare. I2 showed mean-reversion half-life varies 50x across grid (1.8 to 91 days). Current shared 128-dim condition gives all 25 cells identical conditioning — model can't differentiate fast-reverting corners from slow-reverting center. Fan-out Linear(128, 25*32) gives each cell its own 32-dim condition vector from the SAME frozen encoder.
target: Suite 7 (regime coverage per cell), spatially-varying dynamics
prediction: Suite 7's 4 failing regime-cell combos should get cell-specific conditioning. Per-cell coverage spread should decrease.
risk: 25*32=800 additional parameters per cell query. May overfit with 4K training samples. Start with cell_cond_dim=16.
implementation: Add cell_condition_head: Linear(bottleneck_dim, n_cells * cell_cond_dim). In FrameDecoder, each cell gets its own condition slice instead of shared condition.

name: H: Fat-tail noise (Student-t)
theory: I4 proved marginal bottleneck is distribution SHAPE (kurtosis/tails), not rank. GT kurtosis ~77 vs Gaussian 3. Orthogonalizing rank-1 samples to rank-5 did NOT improve Wasserstein. Student-t noise (df=4-6) produces heavier tails naturally, matching GT's fat-tailed per-cell daily change distributions.
prediction: Per-cell kurtosis ratio should improve. KS daily should increase from 20/25. Student-t with df=4 has kurtosis=inf (too heavy) — df=6 gives kurtosis=6 (closer to GT).
risk: Student-t config option already exists (noise_dist='student_t', student_t_df=4.0) but was never tested with the full 99m_v2 recipe. May interact badly with cell_var_loss.
implementation: Just add --noise_dist student_t --student_t_df 6.0 to 99m_v2 training command. Zero code changes needed.

name: I: Explicit mean-reversion in AR decoder (per-cell theta)
theory: I2 showed the FrameDecoder MLP does NOT learn mean-reversion (model ACF=+0.16 vs GT=-0.37). Instead of one-shot (Direction F), add explicit per-cell mean-reversion: delta += theta_head(condition) * (mu_head(condition) - prev). Unlike Exp 104a which had a single alpha, this has PER-CELL theta learned from condition, matching I2 finding that half-life varies 50x. Also cap alpha smaller (0.05 vs 104a's 0.2) to avoid kurtosis collapse.
target: Suite 2 (over-spread from positive ACF), mean-reversion dynamics
prediction: Model ACF should shift negative. VR at h=30 should decrease. Kurtosis should be preserved (smaller alpha cap).
risk: 104a showed mean-reversion dampens tails. Smaller alpha + per-cell theta may avoid this, but uncertain.
implementation: Modify 104a code: mr_mu_head stays (128→25), replace single mr_alpha_head(128→1) with per-cell mr_theta_head(128→25). Cap at 0.05 instead of 0.2.
